scope: Numbers 19–24, all 182 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Numbers 19–24 aligns directly with Hebrew Numbers 19–24. All 182 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps both recipients as the ritual instruction begins.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses and Aaron these instructions:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves female animal, color, soundness and never-yoked condition; does not add a no-calving requirement.
verses.before: “This is the statute of the instruction that the LORD has commanded: Speak to the Israelites and have them bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish and upon which no yoke has ever come.
verses.after: “This is the requirement of the instruction the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red cow, sound and without defect, that has never carried a yoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is the statute of the instruction that the LORD has commanded: Speak to the Israelites and have them bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish and upon which no yoke has ever come.

verses.rationale: Passive English leaves unnamed handlers unspecified; Eleazar supervises outside camp rather than necessarily slaughtering himself.
verses.before: You will give it to Eleazar the priest, and it will be taken outside the camp and slaughtered before him.
verses.after: Give her to Eleazar the priest. She is to be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall give it to Eleazar the priest, and it shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered before him.

verses.rationale: Retains finger, seven repetitions and direction toward the tent rather than onto its fabric.
verses.before: Eleazar the priest will take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.
verses.after: Eleazar the priest must take some of her blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.

verses.rationale: Preserves every burned component, including blood and dung, and supervision by sight.
verses.before: Then the heifer will be burned before his eyes—its hide, flesh, blood, and dung will be burned.
verses.after: The cow must be burned before his eyes—her hide, flesh, blood and dung together.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the heifer shall be burned before his eyes—its hide, flesh, blood, and dung shall be burned.

verses.rationale: Retains all three additions without symbolic meanings inserted into the text.
verses.before: The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material and throw them into the burning of the heifer.
verses.after: The priest must take cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet yarn and throw them into the fire burning the cow.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material and throw them into the burning of the heifer.

verses.rationale: Keeps permission to return before evening distinct from continuing ritual impurity.
verses.before: Then the priest will wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but he remains unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves burner’s separate washing duties and evening endpoint; generic person remains inclusive.
verses.before: The one who burns it will wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water and will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: The person who burns her must also wash their clothes in water and bathe their body in water, and will remain unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who burns it shall wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water and shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains clean male collector and outside storage; contextual purification rendering of hattat is explained rather than forced into ordinary altar sacrifice.
verses.before: A man who is clean will gather up the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They will be kept for the congregation of the Israelites for water of purification; it is for purification from sin.
verses.after: A clean man must gather the cow’s ashes and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They are to be kept for the Israelite community to make water for removing impurity. It is a purification offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the Israelites for water of purification; it is for purification from sin.

verses.rationale: Preserves collector’s resulting impurity and equal resident-foreigner obligation.
verses.before: The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer will wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This will be a perpetual statute for the Israelites and for the resident alien who lives among them.
verses.after: The person who gathers the cow’s ashes must wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This is a lasting rule for the Israelites and the foreigner living among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual statute for the Israelites and for the resident alien who lives among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps human corpse and seven-day duration without equating impurity with personal wrongdoing.
verses.before: Whoever touches the dead body of any person will be unclean seven days.
verses.after: Anyone who touches a human corpse will be unclean for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches the dead body of any person shall be unclean seven days.

verses.rationale: Follows Hebrew clause division; note explains possible attachment of seventh day to purification and verse 19’s explicit two sprinklings.
verses.before: That person will purify themselves with the water on the third day and on the seventh day and will be clean. But if the person does not purify themselves on the third day and on the seventh day, the person will not be clean.
verses.after: They must purify themselves with this water on the third day, and on the seventh day they will be clean. If they do not purify themselves on the third day, they will not be clean on the seventh day.
verses.tsw_comparator: That person shall purify themselves with the water on the third day and on the seventh day and shall be clean. But if the person does not purify themselves on the third day and on the seventh day, the person shall not be clean.

verses.rationale: Keeps sanctuary defilement, severe cut-off consequence and repeated continuing impurity without specifying an unstated execution mechanism.
verses.before: Whoever touches a dead body, the body of a person who has died, and does not purify themselves defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person will be cut off from Israel. Because the water of purification was not sprinkled on them, they remain unclean; their uncleanness is still upon them.
verses.after: Anyone who touches a dead human body and does not purify themselves defiles the LORD’s tabernacle. That person must be cut off from Israel. Because the water for removing impurity was not sprinkled on them, they remain unclean; their impurity is still on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever touches a dead body, the body of a person who has died, and does not purify themselves defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of purification was not sprinkled on them, they remain unclean; their uncleanness is still upon them.

verses.rationale: Makes entering and already-present groups clear while retaining tent setting and duration.
verses.before: This is the instruction when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in the tent will be unclean seven days.
verses.after: This is the instruction when someone dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in it will be unclean for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the instruction when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in the tent shall be unclean seven days.

verses.rationale: Preserves open vessel and absence of a secured covering rather than specifying an invented material.
verses.before: Every open vessel that has no covering fastened over it will be unclean.
verses.after: Every open container without a cover fastened over it will be unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every open vessel that has no covering fastened over it shall be unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains all four contact categories, sword death and open-country setting.
verses.before: Whoever in the open field touches someone killed by the sword, a dead body, a human bone, or a grave will be unclean seven days.
verses.after: Anyone in the open country who touches someone killed by a sword, another dead body, a human bone or a grave will be unclean for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever in the open field touches someone killed by the sword, a dead body, a human bone, or a grave shall be unclean seven days.

verses.rationale: Renders living water as fresh, with source image noted; preserves ashes and container rather than a running-water bath.
verses.before: For the unclean person they will take some of the ashes from the burning of the purification offering and put fresh water with them in a vessel.
verses.after: For an unclean person, take some ashes from the burned purification offering and add fresh water to them in a container.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the unclean person they shall take some of the ashes from the burning of the purification offering and put fresh water with them in a vessel.

verses.rationale: Keeps clean male agent and complete set of objects and people sprinkled. Consistency self-check: The Hebrew kol-hakkelim covers all articles or implements, not only containers. The narrower container sense belongs to the open vessels in 19:15; 31:20 likewise names several kinds of articles.
verses.before: A clean person will take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, all the vessels, the people who were there, and the one who touched the bone, the slain person, the dead body, or the grave.
verses.after: A clean man must take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the articles in it and the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who touched a human bone, someone killed, another dead body or a grave.
verses.tsw_comparator: A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, all the vessels, the people who were there, and the one who touched the bone, the slain person, the dead body, or the grave.

consistency_revisions.rationale: The Hebrew kol-hakkelim covers all articles or implements, not only containers. The narrower container sense belongs to the open vessels in 19:15; 31:20 likewise names several kinds of articles.

verses.rationale: Makes changed subject of washing explicit and retains both sprinkling days plus evening completion.
verses.before: The clean person will sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day the unclean person will purify themselves, wash their clothes, and bathe in water, and at evening will be clean.
verses.after: The clean person must sprinkle the unclean person on the third and seventh days, purifying them on the seventh day. The person being purified must wash their clothes and bathe in water; at evening they will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day the unclean person shall purify themselves, wash their clothes, and bathe in water, and at evening shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated sanction and sanctuary wording rather than deleting it as redundant.
verses.before: But anyone who is unclean and does not purify themselves—that person will be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because that person has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on them; they are unclean.
verses.after: Anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify themselves must be cut off from the assembly for defiling the LORD’s sanctuary. The water for removing impurity has not been sprinkled on them; they are unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: But anyone who is unclean and does not purify themselves—that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because that person has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on them; they are unclean.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct sprinkler-washing and toucher-evening clauses without adding an unstated evening penalty to the sprinkler.
verses.before: It will be a perpetual statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification will wash their clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: This is a lasting rule for them. The person who sprinkles the water for removing impurity must wash their clothes, and anyone who touches that water will be unclean until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a perpetual statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash their clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains secondary transmission with its shorter evening duration, not an automatic seven-day reset.
verses.before: Whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and the person who touches it will be unclean until evening.
verses.after: Whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

verses.rationale: Keeps first month without supplying an unstated year; preserves both death and burial of Miriam.
verses.before: The Israelites, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
verses.after: In the first month, the Israelites—the whole community—came to the wilderness of Zin and stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.

verses.rationale: Retains the actual lack of water as the setting for opposition.
verses.before: Now there was no water for the congregation, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
verses.after: There was no water for the community, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was no water for the congregation, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.

verses.rationale: Renders generic brothers as own people without choosing which earlier deaths the speakers mean.
verses.before: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished when our brothers perished before the LORD!
verses.after: The people argued with Moses. “If only we had died when our own people died before the LORD!” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished when our brothers perished before the LORD!

verses.rationale: Keeps the community’s LORD-assembly claim and both human and animal need.
verses.before: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?
verses.after: “Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?

verses.rationale: Preserves four crops and drinking-water lack, without turning the complaint into a narrator’s agricultural survey.
verses.before: Why have you brought us up from Egypt to bring us to this evil place? It is no place for seed, figs, vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”
verses.after: Why did you bring us up from Egypt to this terrible place? There is nowhere to grow grain, figs, vines or pomegranates—and no water to drink!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why have you brought us up from Egypt to bring us to this evil place? It is no place for seed, figs, vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies movement away from people and retains both leaders’ posture and divine appearance.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and fell on their faces. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the entrance of the tent of meeting. They fell facedown, and the LORD’s glory appeared to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and fell on their faces. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

verses.rationale: Marks singular recipient before the command that includes Aaron.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps take-staff versus speak-to-rock distinction, visible action and provision for animals; staff identity remains unasserted.
verses.before: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. You will bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.”
verses.after: “Take the staff and gather the community, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. Bring water out of the rock for them, and give the community and their livestock a drink.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water. You shall bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.”

verses.rationale: Preserves location of staff and command compliance before the subsequent disputed action.
verses.before: So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as the LORD commanded him.
verses.after: Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as he had commanded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as the LORD commanded him.

verses.rationale: Makes singular speaker Moses clear, retaining we and the rebels accusation without inserting a motive.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Will we bring water for you out of this rock?”
verses.after: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock. Moses said, “Listen, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”

verses.rationale: Keeps two blows and abundant water despite the leaders’ failure; no invented failure of the miracle.
verses.before: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
verses.after: Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water poured out, and the community and their livestock drank.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their livestock drank.

verses.rationale: Preserves both men’s responsibility and stated trust/holiness reason without reducing it to only striking twice.
verses.before: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust me, to treat me as holy in the eyes of the Israelites, therefore you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses and Aaron, “You did not trust me enough to show my holiness before the Israelites’ eyes. So you will not bring this assembly into the land I have given them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust me, to treat me as holy in the eyes of the Israelites, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”

verses.rationale: Retains dispute/holiness connection; note leaves among-them versus through-waters grammatical reference open.
verses.before: These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD and the LORD showed holiness among them.
verses.after: These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites argued with the LORD and he showed his holiness among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD and the LORD showed holiness among them.

verses.rationale: Preserves Israel’s brother address to Edom and message provenance.
verses.before: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has found us,
verses.after: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship we have faced.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has found us,

verses.rationale: Retains both generations suffering and long duration without inserting a number of years.
verses.before: how our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many years, and the Egyptians treated us and our ancestors badly.
verses.after: Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: how our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many years, and the Egyptians treated us and our ancestors badly.

verses.rationale: Keeps angel/messenger agency as stated without identifying the figure; preserves border location.
verses.before: But when we cried to the LORD, the LORD heard our voice, sent a messenger, and brought us out from Egypt. And look, we are at Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.
verses.after: We cried out to the LORD. He heard our voice, sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when we cried to the LORD, the LORD heard our voice, sent a messenger, and brought us out from Egypt. And look, we are at Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.

verses.rationale: Retains three restrictions, named road and both directions as the diplomatic offer.
verses.before: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, nor drink water from a well. We will go by the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
verses.after: Please let us pass through your land. We will not cross fields or vineyards or drink water from wells. We will stay on the King’s Highway, turning neither right nor left until we have passed through your territory.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, nor drink water from a well. We will go by the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Edom as collective speaker and explicit sword threat.
verses.before: Yet Edom said to him, “You will not pass through me, or I will come out against you with the sword.”
verses.after: Edom answered, “You must not pass through my land, or I will come out against you with the sword.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through me, or I will come out against you with the sword.”

verses.rationale: Preserves revised conditional water offer rather than harmonizing it with the earlier no-water promise.
verses.before: The Israelites said to him, “We will go up by the highway, and if we or our livestock drink your water, we will pay its price. Only let us pass through on foot—nothing more.”
verses.after: The Israelites replied, “We will stay on the main road. If we or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We ask only to pass through on foot.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites said to him, “We will go up by the highway, and if we or our livestock drink your water, we will pay its price. Only let us pass through on foot—nothing more.”

verses.rationale: Conveys emphatic refusal and retains strong-hand image alongside sizable force.
verses.before: But he said, “You will not pass through.” And Edom came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.
verses.after: “No passage!” Edom said, and came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “You shall not pass through.” And Edom came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps refusal and withdrawal instead of importing a conquest here.
verses.before: Thus Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
verses.after: Edom refused to let Israel cross its territory, so Israel turned away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated whole-community scope and both locations.
verses.before: The Israelites, the whole congregation, set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
verses.after: The Israelites—the whole community—left Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites, the whole congregation, set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.

verses.rationale: Retains Edom boundary and both recipients before Aaron’s death announcement.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying,
verses.after: At Mount Hor, on the border of Edom, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps gathered-to-people idiom and plural culpability; does not turn the idiom into a physical burial claim.
verses.before: “Aaron will be gathered to his people, for he will not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
verses.after: “Aaron will be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land I have given the Israelites, because you both rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.

verses.rationale: Retains father/son relationship and ascent required for transfer of office.
verses.before: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up Mount Hor.
verses.after: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up Mount Hor.

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing transfer and both gathering/death clauses without embellishing ceremony.
verses.before: Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron will be gathered and will die there.”
verses.after: Remove Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and die there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron shall be gathered and shall die there.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public visibility of ascent without implying the whole community accompanied them.
verses.before: Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor before the eyes of the whole congregation.
verses.after: Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor before the eyes of the whole community.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor before the eyes of the whole congregation.

verses.rationale: Preserves succession, summit death and two returnees distinctly.
verses.before: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
verses.after: Moses removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on the mountaintop, and Moses and Eleazar came down the mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

verses.rationale: Retains communal grief, thirty days and whole-house scope.
verses.before: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
verses.after: When the whole community saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for him for thirty days.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.

verses.rationale: Keeps attacker, approach route and actual captives; route-name uncertainty is noted.
verses.before: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
verses.after: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road of Atharim. He fought Israel and took some of them captive.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional vow and religiously dedicated destruction without euphemism or modern justification.
verses.before: Israel vowed a vow to the LORD and said, “If you surely give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction.”
verses.after: Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If you will indeed give these people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel vowed a vow to the LORD and said, “If you surely give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction.”

verses.rationale: Keeps human and urban destruction, divine attribution and naming wordplay.
verses.before: The LORD listened to the voice of Israel and gave the Canaanites into their hand. They devoted them and their cities to destruction, and the name of the place was called Hormah.
verses.after: The LORD heard Israel’s voice and gave them the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction, and the place was named Hormah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD listened to the voice of Israel and gave the Canaanites into their hand. They devoted them and their cities to destruction, and the name of the place was called Hormah.

verses.rationale: Retains bypass route and renders shortened-nephesh idiom as exhausted patience.
verses.before: And they set out from Mount Hor by the way to the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom, and the soul of the people grew short on the way.

verses.rationale: Keeps both addressees and apparent no-bread/this-food tension within the complaint.

verses.rationale: Retains fiery designation and lethal bites; notes possible burning venom sense without choosing a modern species.

verses.rationale: Preserves confession, requested removal and Moses’ intercession without claiming all snakes were removed.

verses.rationale: Retains made snake-image and conditional looking/living, without importing later interpretation into the command.

verses.rationale: Keeps bronze material, repeated snake language and enacted result; vocabulary notes Hebrew soundplay.
verses.before: So Moses made a serpent of bronze and set it on the pole. And if a serpent bit anyone, and he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.
verses.after: Moses made a bronze snake and put it on the pole. When a snake bit someone, that person looked at the bronze snake and lived.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses made a serpent of bronze and set it on the pole. And if a serpent bit anyone, and he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

verses.rationale: Preserves first named stop without adding route coordinates.

verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Israel set out and camped at Oboth.

verses.rationale: Retains location facing Moab and eastward sunrise image.

verses.after: From Oboth they traveled to Iye-abarim and camped in the wilderness facing Moab, toward the sunrise.

verses.tsw_comparator: From there they set out and camped in the Wadi Zered.

verses.rationale: Retains boundary explanation and relative beyond wording rather than inventing a map location.

verses.after: Then they moved on and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness extending from Amorite territory. The Arnon is Moab’s boundary, between Moab and the Amorites.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites, for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

verses.rationale: Preserves fragmentary poetic quotation without inventing a missing verb; names versus storm interpretation noted.

verses.tsw_comparator: and the slope of the wadis that extends toward the dwelling of Ar and leans upon the border of Moab.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Beer/well linkage and recalled divine water promise.
verses.before: From there they went to Beer. This is the well of which the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people, and I will give them water.”

verses.rationale: Keeps diplomatic initiative before battle without importing the other witnesses’ words-of-peace phrase.

verses.rationale: Retains refusal, complete force and location, making repeated subject clear.

verses.rationale: Keeps sword violence, both rivers and strong boundary; does not emend strong to Jazer.

verses.rationale: Renders daughter-towns relationally while retaining conquest and settlement.
verses.before: Israel took all these cities, and Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its towns.

verses.rationale: Preserves prior conquest explaining possession and does not add moral justification for either war.

verses.after: Heshbon had been the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and had taken all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon.

verses.rationale: Introduces mashal singers’ quoted poem with its rebuilding invitation and parallel verbs.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned lords reading rather than emending to a second consumed verb; keeps fire imagery.
verses.before: For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
verses.after: Fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon’s city. It consumed Ar of Moab and the lords of the Arnon’s heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.

verses.rationale: Retains Chemosh as poem’s agency, specifically sons/daughters and forced displacement.

verses.after: Woe to you, Moab! You are lost, people of Chemosh! He made his sons fugitives and his daughters captives of Sihon king of the Amorites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.

verses.rationale: Follows difficult pinned shooting/relative readings with uncertainty noted; retains extraordinary dot in source hash, not silently replacing which with fire.
verses.before: We shot them down; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon; we laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
verses.after: We shot them down; Heshbon perished as far as Dibon. We laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We shot them down; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon; we laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”

verses.rationale: Keeps narrative resumption after the quoted victory poem.
verses.before: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
verses.after: So Israel settled in Amorite territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.

verses.rationale: Returns the final singular verb to Moses after the plural capture; follows the read causative form for dispossession. Both written and read forms are singular, with a stem difference, and are hashed exactly.
verses.before: Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they captured its towns and dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
verses.after: Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. They captured its surrounding villages, and Moses drove out the Amorites there.

verses.rationale: Retains route, king, all people and battle location.

verses.after: They turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out with all his people to fight them at Edrei.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

verses.rationale: Keeps three objects given and explicit Sihon comparison without adding a claim about a particular age group.

verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him. I have given him, all his people and his land into your hand. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have given him and all his people and his land into your hand. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”

verses.rationale: Preserves no-survivor claim and sons instead of softening to a mere military defeat.
verses.before: So they struck him and his sons and all his people until no survivor remained to him, and they possessed his land.
verses.after: They struck down Og, his sons and all his people, leaving him no survivor. Then they took possession of his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they struck him and his sons and all his people until no survivor remained to him, and they possessed his land.

verses.rationale: Keeps travel and the narrator’s Jordan-side orientation without relocating the camp west of the river.
verses.before: The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan from Jericho.
verses.after: The Israelites set out and camped on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan from Jericho.

verses.rationale: Introduces Balak through his observation of the preceding victories.
verses.before: Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
verses.after: Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.

verses.rationale: Preserves the grazing image and the narrator’s separate identification of Balak’s office.

verses.rationale: Retains the ambiguous land-of-his-people wording and River designation; does not silently substitute Amaw or an inferred precise location.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift from plural striking to singular driving out and the paired blessing/curse claim.

verses.rationale: Keeps overnight consultation and the explicit Moabite identity of those remaining.

verses.rationale: Preserves the question rather than explaining God’s knowledge or motive.

verses.after: God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”

verses.rationale: Identifies the speaker and the quoted message’s origin before the embedded speech.

verses.rationale: Retains the shorter retelling and its singular first-person verbs rather than harmonizing it with verses 5–6.

verses.rationale: Keeps both prohibitions and the stated reason tied to the people’s blessing.

verses.rationale: Does not add the blessing explanation that Balaam leaves out of his reply.

verses.rationale: Retains both escalation in number and rank.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ordinary departure before the unexpected confrontation.

verses.tsw_comparator: Water flows from their buckets, and their seed is in abundant waters. Their king shall be higher than Agag, and their kingdom shall be exalted.

verses.rationale: Retains singular pronouns, wild ox and violent victory images; arrows clause is difficult and its rendering is noted rather than silently emended.
verses.before: God brings them out of Egypt; they have strength like the horns of a wild ox. They will devour nations, their adversaries, and crush their bones, and shatter them with arrows.
verses.after: God brings him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He devours the nations that oppose him, crushes their bones and pierces them with his arrows.
verses.tsw_comparator: God brings them out of Egypt; they have strength like the horns of a wild ox. They shall devour nations, their adversaries, and crush their bones, and shatter them with arrows.

verses.rationale: Keeps both lion terms, the challenge and familiar paired blessing/curse wording that connects earlier promises.
verses.before: They crouch, they lie down like a lion, and like a lioness—who will rouse them? Blessed are people who bless you, and cursed are people who curse you.”
verses.after: He crouches and lies down like a lion, like a lioness—who would rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you!”
verses.tsw_comparator: They crouch, they lie down like a lion, and like a lioness—who will rouse them? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the bodily gesture and counted threefold reversal without inventing its exact gesture convention.
verses.before: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look—you have blessed them these three times!
verses.after: Balak burned with anger at Balaam and struck his hands together. He said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, and here you have blessed them these three times!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look—you have blessed them these three times!

verses.rationale: Retains the expulsion and Balak’s attribution of lost honor to the LORD as quoted accusation.
verses.before: Now flee to your place. I said I would honor you greatly, but look—the LORD has kept you from honor.”
verses.after: Now get away! Go home! I said I would give you great honor, but the LORD has kept you from that honor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now flee to your place. I said I would honor you greatly, but look—the LORD has kept you from honor.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the introduction to Balaam’s repeated earlier response; sentence continues across the verse label.
verses.before: Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,
verses.after: Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell the messengers you sent me,
verses.tsw_comparator: Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the retelling’s good/bad pair and own-initiative qualification rather than harmonizing with 22:18’s small/great pair.
verses.before: ‘Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot cross the command of the LORD to do good or evil from my own heart. What the LORD speaks, that I will speak’?
verses.after: ‘Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the LORD’s command to do good or bad on my own. Whatever the LORD says, I will say’?
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot cross the command of the LORD to do good or evil from my own heart. What the LORD speaks, that I will speak’?

verses.rationale: Keeps the future action directed against Balak’s people; days to come does not impose a specific end-times system.
verses.before: And now, look, I am going to my people. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people in days to come.”
verses.after: Now I am going back to my people. Come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in days to come.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, look, I am going to my people. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people in days to come.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated identification and eye formula with the same lexical decision as verse 3.
verses.before: Then he took up his oracle and said: “The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
verses.after: Then he took up his oracle: “The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he took up his oracle and said: “The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,

verses.rationale: Keeps the added knowledge line, both divine titles and the repeated falling/eyes language without an unmarked trance claim.
verses.before: the declaration of one who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, yet with eyes uncovered:
verses.after: who hears the words of God, who knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision of the Almighty, falling down, with eyes uncovered:
verses.tsw_comparator: the declaration of one who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, yet with eyes uncovered:

verses.rationale: Retains distant vision, star and scepter; chooses head-temples for corners, preserves pinned qarqar as devastate and uncertain Sheth as a name rather than silently emending the line.
verses.before: I see him, but not now; I look him, but not near. A star comes out from Jacob, and a scepter rises from Israel. It crushes the temples of Moab and breaks down all the sons of Seth.
verses.after: I see him, but not now; I look at him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob, a scepter will rise from Israel. He will crush Moab’s temples and devastate all the descendants of Sheth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star comes out from Jacob, and a scepter rises from Israel. It crushes the temples of Moab and breaks down all the sons of Seth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated possession claim and treats the plural enemies as a collective description of Seir, without changing the territorial object.
verses.before: Edom becomes a possession, Seir becomes a possession of its enemies, while Israel acts with strength.
verses.after: Edom will become a possession; his enemy Seir will become a possession, while Israel acts with strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Edom becomes a possession, Seir becomes a possession of its enemies, while Israel acts with strength.

verses.rationale: Retains the unnamed city and survivor-destruction claim rather than inserting a modern or otherwise inferred city.
verses.before: One from Jacob will rule and destroy the survivors from the city.”
verses.after: One from Jacob will rule and destroy the survivors from the city.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One from Jacob shall rule and destroy the survivors from the city.”

verses.rationale: Preserves first without specifying chronological origin or political ranking, and keeps the first/end contrast.
verses.before: Then Balaam saw Amalek, took up his oracle, and said: “First among the nations was Amalek, but its end is destruction.”
verses.after: Then he saw Amalek and took up his oracle: “Amalek was first among the nations, but its end will be destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Balaam saw Amalek, took up his oracle, and said: “First among the nations was Amalek, but its end is destruction.”

verses.rationale: Retains nest and rock imagery addressed to the Kenites, preparing the Kain wordplay.
verses.before: Then he saw the Kenites, took up his oracle, and said: “Enduring is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock;
verses.after: Then he saw the Kenites and took up his oracle: “Your dwelling is secure; your nest is set in the rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he saw the Kenites, took up his oracle, and said: “Enduring is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock;

verses.rationale: Preserves Kain and Asshur names, retaining the difficult time-question rather than forcing a certain identification of Asshur or a duration.
verses.before: even so Kain will be consumed. How long until Asshur carries you captive?”
verses.after: Yet Kain will be consumed. How long until Asshur takes you captive?”
verses.tsw_comparator: nevertheless Kain shall be consumed. How long until Asshur carries you captive?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the lament and question about survival without assigning an unexpressed modern event.
verses.before: Then he took up his oracle and said: “Alas! Who will live when God does this?
verses.after: Then he took up his oracle: “Alas! Who can live when God brings this about?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he took up his oracle and said: “Alas! Who shall live when God does this?

verses.rationale: Preserves Kittim, both oppressed names and the final singular pronoun’s uncertain referent rather than resolving the historical sequence dogmatically.
verses.before: Ships will come from the coast of Kittim; they will afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and they too will come to destruction.”
verses.after: Ships will come from the coast of Kittim. They will oppress Asshur and oppress Eber; he too will end in destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ships will come from the coast of Kittim; they will afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and they too shall come to destruction.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both departures as this scene’s conclusion without importing later events to harmonize the account.
verses.before: Then Balaam rose and went and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way.
verses.after: Then Balaam got up, left and returned to his own place. Balak also went on his way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Balaam rose and went and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way.
